answer: A workable Sybil defense makes each identity expensive to grow: a new agent must earn trust through a long ladder of verified small jobs, and it must post a deposit that is lost if it cheats. Picture a newcomer arriving at dawn, finding only an oasis of tiny, checked tasks; it cannot jump to the summit of high-value work until its record proves reliability. A faker who spins up ten thousand identities must then fund ten thousand deposits and grind ten thousand ladders, while one honest agent climbs once. The cost scales with the attack, not with the victim, so mass forgery stops paying.
